column2: The two deaths are repeated in the source, with strange fire explicitly named. The awkward repetition is preserved rather than shortened from memory.
Entry within the veil is restricted, with death and the cloud appearance as reasons. Propitiatory cover remains the established provisional hilasterion term.
A calf for sin and a ram for the whole offering specify how Aaron approaches. The two offering roles are distinct.
Four linen items and bathing the whole body precede dressing. Holy garments is an explicit explanation, not an added devotional title.
The congregation supplies two male goats and one ram. These gifts remain distinct from Aaron's own calf.
Aaron presents his calf and makes atonement for himself and his house. House is retained, not replaced by the wider congregation.
Both goats are set before the Lord beside the entrance. Their initial shared presentation precedes the divergent lots.
One lot is for the Lord and one for apopompaios. The inherited one sent away is provisional; no Hebrew name is inserted.
column3: Does apopompaios denote the dismissed animal, removal, or an averting recipient? Specialist lexical and apparatus work remains open.

column2: The goat assigned to the Lord is presented for sin. The relative clause identifies it by the lot, not by physical characteristics.
The other goat remains alive for atonement over it and dismissal into the wilderness. Removal and release remain distinct expressions.
Alone is explicitly supported by monon and limits the calf's stated scope to Aaron and his house here.
Firepan coals come from the altar, and hands are filled with finely compounded incense. The plural hands is not reduced to one handful.
Incense vapour covers the propitiatory above the testimonies, preventing death. The plural testimonies is retained.
Eastward sprinkling on the cover and seven sprinklings before it are separately described. The number is not indiscriminately attached to both clauses.
The people's goat blood follows the calf-blood procedure. Both on and before the cover remain rather than forcing a single reconstructed gesture.
Atonement concerns the sanctuary in relation to uncleanness, wrongdoing and all sins. The tent is established amid their uncleanness.
No one else occupies the tent during the priest's entrance-to-exit interval. His atonement includes himself, household and entire congregation.
Calf and goat blood are applied around the altar horns. Upon it retains the preposition in the atonement clause provisionally.
Seven finger sprinklings precede cleansing and consecration from Israel's uncleannesses. Both verbs and their common object remain.
The Greek includes cleansing concerning the priests before the living goat is brought. This clause is not omitted as absent in another base.
All lawlessness, injustice and sins are confessed, with all repeated. A prepared man conveys the goat; no official title is invented.
The goat bears injustices to inaccessible land; the following he releases it shifts to an implicit human agent.
column3: Should the releasing man be named for clarity, or would that overresolve the implicit subject?

column2: Aaron removes the linen robe previously worn for entering and leaves it there. The temporal relationship is retained.
Bathing and redressing precede whole offerings and atonement. The final comparison concerning the priests is retained despite its interpretive difficulty.
column3: What is the exact scope of as for the priests in the final atonement clause?

column2: The fat belongs to offerings for sins, expressed in the plural. The short instruction is not expanded with unstated organs.
The releaser washes garments and bathes before entering camp. The goat is described as designated for release, avoiding an imported proper name.
Plural workers carry and burn calf and goat outside camp, including hides, flesh and dung. Their blood's prior sanctuary use identifies the animals.
The burner washes and bathes before returning. May enter represents resulting permission; it does not add a new agent.
Seventh month, tenth day, self-humbling and no work apply to native and resident foreigner. No explicit fasting verb is supplied.
Atonement cleanses from all sins before the Lord. The unnamed singular actor remains he rather than an inserted divine subject.
Sabbath of Sabbaths, rest, self-humbling and enduring statute remain. The emphatic Sabbath construction is not reduced to a generic holiday.
Unnamed plural agents anoint and consecrate the successor after his father. Hands preserves the consecration idiom; the linen robe is called holy.
Sanctuary, tent and altar precede priests and congregation in the repeated atonement clauses. The repeated verb is retained.
The selected Greek ends with a passive annual performance requirement. Once in the year is not changed into a narrated past act by Aaron.
Moses receives the speech introducing slaughter and blood regulations. The command is addressed onward in verse 2.
Aaron, his sons and all Israel are explicitly addressed. The broad audience is not narrowed to priests alone.
The distributive person formula includes resident foreigners in this Greek verse. Calf, sheep and goat, and inside/outside camp remain distinct.
The longer Greek condition includes both offering types and repeated failure to bring the gift. Blood reckoning and destruction remain; no shorter base is substituted.
Field sacrifices are to be brought to the Lord and priest as deliverance sacrifices. The emphatic they themselves is supported.
The priest pours blood around the altar and offers fat for a sweet savour. The tent-door location is explicit.
Vain things renders the Greek mataioi provisionally; goat demons is not imported. The prostitution metaphor remains in the description of their following.
column3: What English label best expresses the contextual objects denoted by mataioi?

column2: The rule expressly includes sons of resident foreigners. The distributive alternatives and whole offering/sacrifice distinction remain.
Failure to bring the offering for the Lord entails removal/destruction from the people. The sanction's mechanism is not specified.
Any blood is prohibited; the Lord explicitly sets His face against and destroys the eater. Divine agency is preserved.
Life is identified with blood, which is given on the altar. In place of preserves anti rather than replacing it with by reason of.
The negative applies to every person and is repeated for the resident foreigner. No soul is idiomatic distributive negation.
Hunted edible animal or bird requires blood poured out and covered with earth. The two actions remain separate.
The life/blood explanation is repeated before the sanction. Its repetition is not removed as redundant theology.
Carcass or prey of beasts applies to native and resident foreigner. Washing, bathing, waiting and clean status remain sequential.
Failure to wash garments and bathe brings responsibility for wrongdoing. Bear retains the burden expression without inventing a specific punishment.
The Lord says to Moses; the saying formula introduces a new set of instructions.
The divine identity statement addresses Israel through Moses. Your is plural; no archaic singular divine-address pronoun is appropriate.
Egyptian and Canaanite practices are separately prohibited, with past residence and future destination distinguished.
Doing judgments, keeping ordinances and walking in them remain related but distinct commands.
All ordinances and all judgments are explicit. Live by them represents en autois provisionally without adding a theological explanation.
The distributive prohibition concerns approaching flesh relatives to uncover nakedness. The sexual idiom remains restrained and source-led.
Father and mother are both named; the following explanation focuses on the mother. The asymmetry is not silently corrected.
The father's wife's nakedness is identified with the father's. The relational identification remains rather than being collapsed.
Paternal or maternal sister, born within or outside, is covered. The birth-location phrases are not converted into an unsupported legal status.
Both a son's daughter and a daughter's daughter are named. Their nakedness is identified with the addressee's own.
The father's wife's daughter is specifically a sister by the same father. That qualification prevents misrepresenting the kinship.
The father's sister is prohibited as his close relative. The father's relationship remains the explanatory focus.
The parallel maternal relationship is separately stated and retained in full.
The paternal uncle and his wife are linked by the two clauses. Relative renders the woman's kinship designation without inserting another technical term.
Daughter-in-law is explained as the son's wife; the prohibition is repeated. Both features remain.
The brother's wife's nakedness is identified with the brother's. No exception is imported from another law.
Woman, daughter and both lines of granddaughter are covered. The Greek says your relatives, which is retained.
Taking a sister as rival is restricted while the other woman lives. The temporal limit remains, without expanding this into a full marriage doctrine.
column3: Confirm each feminine pronoun's referent in a final syntax review.

column2: Approach during separation for uncleanness is prohibited. No modern diagnosis or extra duration is added.
The neighbour's wife, emission and defilement are explicit. The English makes the intercourse idiom intelligible without adding motive.
The Greek says serve a ruler and the holy name. No Molech name or fire ritual is inserted into this wording.
column3: Does archon require a more specific contextual gloss, while preserving the selected Greek rather than substituting Hebrew?

column2: The prohibition uses male and the woman's lying idiom. The inherited comparative English is retained without importing modern identity terminology.
Both male intercourse with a quadruped and a woman being mounted are prohibited. The descriptive language remains restrained.
All these practices are connected with the prior nations' defilement. The Lord's driving them out is explicitly first-person.
The land becomes indignant in this Greek text. Vomiting imagery is not substituted; repayment is directed to them.
All statutes and commands apply to native and joined resident foreigner. The prohibition concerns any of the listed abominations.
The prior inhabitants and their acts explain the land's defilement. The parenthetic position preserves the argument into verse 28.
Indignation of the land is repeated, comparing the present audience with former nations. The metaphor remains consistent with verse 25.
The singular anyone leads to plural souls doing these acts. The English preserves that distribution without defining the sanction's procedure.
Keeping ordinances prevents the former abominable practices and defilement. The final divine identity remains part of the command's rationale.
The Lord addresses Moses as intermediary for the congregational instructions.
The congregation is commanded to be holy because the Lord is holy. No separate explanatory moral category is added.
Father precedes mother in this Greek text; revere conveys the respect-context fear verb. Sabbath keeping is a separate plural command.
Following idols and making cast gods are both forbidden. The manufacture detail is retained.
The deliverance sacrifice must be acceptable for the offerers. The genitive relation remains provisional rather than turned into freewill wording.
Eating is allowed on sacrifice day and the next, with burning on the third. The day count is explicit.
At all reflects emphatic paired eating forms. Unfit for sacrifice represents athyton, followed by rejection.
The eater bears sin because holy things are profaned. The Greek shifts to plural eaters in the destruction clause.
The harvest must not be exhausted, and fallen produce must not be collected. A field corner is not inserted where this Greek does not name it.
Again is supported by the repeated-harvest verb. The grapes remain broadly named, with poor and resident foreigner as beneficiaries.
column3: Does rhogas here specifically imply fallen or remaining individual grapes in context?

column2: Stealing, lying and defrauding the neighbour are distinct prohibitions. Sycophancy's modern flattery sense is not imposed on sykophanteo.
The oath is prohibited for an unjust cause; profaning God's name is separately stated. Both divine identity and plural addressee remain.
Wronging, robbing and withholding wages overnight are separately prohibited. The emphatic negative is represented without adding a new time limit.
Speaking evil of the deaf and placing an obstacle before the blind remain concrete prohibitions, followed by fear of God.
Judgment must favour neither poor nor powerful. Person language retains the face idiom while righteousness governs judgment.
Deceitful conduct and conspiring against a neighbour's blood are separate. The Greek wording is not changed into a bystander rule without evidence.
Hatred in the mind is forbidden; emphatic reproof and not bearing sin because of the neighbour follow. The causal phrase remains open.
column3: Does because of him or on his account best convey the final relation?

column2: The source explicitly names your hand in vengeance. Lasting anger is prohibited before the command to love the neighbour as oneself.
Livestock mating, vineyard sowing and mixed woven clothing are distinct restrictions. Vineyard, not field, is the selected Greek reading.
The woman is enslaved and reserved for a man, lacking ransom or freedom. Inquiry renders episkope provisionally; the text denies death because she is unfreed.
column3: Does episkope here mean judicial inquiry, punishment or visitation? Specialist review must resolve this material legal term.

column2: The man brings a ram for guilt at the tent entrance. His required action is not assigned to the woman.
The priest makes atonement for him with the ram, and forgiveness concerns his committed sin. The repeated sin phrase remains.
The fruit is unpurged for three years, with no eating. The Greek purification vocabulary is retained rather than replaced with an uncircumcision metaphor.
All fourth-year fruit is holy and praiseworthy to the Lord. The unusual adjective remains pending contextual refinement.
column3: Does ainenetos imply praiseworthy fruit or fruit dedicated in praise here?

column2: Fifth-year eating and increased produce follow the prior restrictions. The promise is not converted into an unstated agricultural technique.
The Greek says mountains, not blood. Omen-taking and bird divination are separately prohibited; the source difference is preserved.
Sisoe remains an unresolved transliteration; the second prohibition concerns damaging the beard's appearance. No specific haircut is guessed.
column3: What English haircut term can be supported for sisoe by specialist lexical evidence?

column2: Incisions for a dead person and tattooed letters are separately named. Letters retains grammata rather than expanding it to every possible image.
The inherited lest construes the linked clauses as a warning of land-wide consequences. The final filling clause lacks its own negative in Greek.
column3: Does the scope of the preceding negative support lest over both outcomes, or should a closer staged alternative display the syntax?

column2: Sabbaths and holy things receive observance and reverence. The plural holy expression is retained without forcing a singular building.
Mediums and enchanters remain two categories, with defilement as the stated consequence. No etymological ventriloquist paraphrase is imposed.
Rising before grey hair, honouring an elder and fearing God are separate commands. The personal object is not reduced to age as an abstraction.
The arriving resident foreigner must not be oppressed. The conditional arrival and land setting remain.
The resident foreigner is treated as native and loved as self, grounded in Israel's Egyptian sojourn. Both comparisons are preserved.
Justice governs judgment, measures, weights and scales. The list is not narrowed to only courtroom justice.
Just scales, weights and a chous are required. The ancient capacity term remains without an invented modern conversion.
All law and all ordinances are to be kept and done. The double all and final divine identity close the chapter.
